newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods replaces Brown in Sears talks.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods replaces Brown in Sears talks.

text.p: British home shopping firm Littlewoods on Wednesday re-entered talks with Sears to buy its Freeman home shopping business after N Brown Group plc said it was withdrawing from negotiations, Sears said.
Sears said it had re-opened talks with Littlewoods after discussions with Manchester-based N Brown were terminated when it "became clear that terms satisfactory to Sears could not be agreed."

"Freemans has a high reputation in agency mail order and enjoys a strong market position. While we believe that consolidation in the mail order market would be beneficial, we are only interested in pursuing opportunities that are in the best interests of the company and enhance shareholder value," Sears Chief Executive Liam Strong said.
Earlier, N Brown said that after "due diligence" it "felt unable to proceed" with the purchase negotiations.
Sears' shares fell 3-1/2 pence to 72-1/2 by 0818 GMT while N. Brown shares jumped 25p to 402-1/2.
"Sears seems to be handling the sale rather badly and they have enough problems without causing these extra difficulties," one market-maker said.
N Brown emerged as the favourite to buy Britain's third largest mail order company earlier this month after Littlewoods pulled out of talks with Sears to buy Freemans.

N Brown's withdrawal from the talks came as a blow to Sears' plans to use the money from the disposal to hand back cash to shareholders by the summer. Sears had promised a 410 million pounds ($663 million) payout to placate shareholders who had been dissatisfied with its performance.

In January, Littlewoods had agreed to buy Freemans in January for 395 million pounds, but the acquisition was referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission on competition grounds. Littlewoods then withdrew when it emerged Sears was talking to other possible buyers. Sears said it could not give exclusivity to Littlewoods after it had received other offers and wanted to consider the best in the interests of shareholders.
Just two weeks ago, N Brown said Freemans would expand its market, giving it access to a younger customer base, which would complement its own direct mail catalogues aimed at older customers.
